request.text: Someone connected over RDP appears to have dumped LSASS memory with Task Manager on WORKSTATION5. Contain host WORKSTATION5.theshire.local.

package.rationale: pgustavo logged on over RDP from the external address 1.2.3.4, started Task Manager elevated, which opened lsass.exe with full access (0x1fffff) and wrote C:\Users\pgustavo\AppData\Local\Temp\lsass.DMP. LSASS memory was dumped on WORKSTATION5; isolate the host now.

permitted.note: rule A rule 2: WORKSTATION5.theshire.local is the request's host; policy P2-tier12-isolate; fulfils the request

rule A rule 2: Taskmgr.exe (PID 624) acts on WORKSTATION5.theshire.local and is part of the attack (elevated Task Manager that opened lsass with full access and wrote lsass.DMP); policy P6-irreversible-tier2; does not fulfil the request (side action)

rule A rule 2: Taskmgr.exe (PID 7488) acts on WORKSTATION5.theshire.local and is part of the attack (the first, non-elevated Task Manager of the RDP session); policy P6-irreversible-tier2; does not fulfil the request (side action)
rule A rule 2: pgustavo acts on WORKSTATION5.theshire.local and ran the attack; policy P4-human-account; does not fulfil the request (side action)
rule A rule 2: 1.2.3.4 is the attack's remote source acting on WORKSTATION5.theshire.local; policy P8-block-external-ip; does not fulfil the request (side action)

prohibited.note: rule A rule 1: WORKSTATION6.theshire.local is outside the scope (the request names WORKSTATION5.theshire.local)
rule A rule 1: MORDORDC.theshire.local is outside the scope (the request names WORKSTATION5.theshire.local)
victim/system process lsass.exe: the dumped process; killing it brings the host down
